servers.description: Tenant Authority, served under the partner's own CYRISMA instance host.

instance.description: The instance label of the tenant host issued to the partner.

post.summary: Exchange an API key for an access token
post.description:
Exchanges an API key for a bearer token, valid for one hour by default. The token is for the
API key's own tenant, and gives access to that tenant and every tenant beneath it.

* **401** (no body): the client id or secret is missing or wrong, or the key has been revoked.
* **403** `tenant_context_denied`: the tenant is not active (for example suspended), or the key has no access left.
* **403** `scope_denied`: `requested_scopes` asks for a scope the key does not hold.

get.description:
Returns the full details of one tenant. Needs `pulse.read`.

* **401** (no body): missing or invalid token, no `pulse.read`, or the tenant is outside your hierarchy.

parameters.name: tenantId
parameters.description: The tenant: a `tenant_id` from **List tenants** (`GET /v1/msp/admin/tenants`). Must be your own tenant or one beneath it.

patch.description:
Changes a tenant's details and returns the updated tenant. Send only the fields to change.
Needs `pulse.write`.

* **400**: a validation problem naming the first invalid field.
* **401** (no body): missing or invalid token, no `pulse.write`, or the tenant is outside your hierarchy.

parameters.name: tenantId
parameters.description: The tenant: a `tenant_id` from **List tenants** (`GET /v1/msp/admin/tenants`). Must be your own tenant or one beneath it.

get.description:
Returns how users of a tenant sign in: MFA requirement, allowed MFA methods and SSO.
**Needs a signed-in user's token.** API-key tokens from `POST /v1/auth/client-token` are rejected. The user needs `pulse.write` and an admin role.

* **401** `invalid_credentials`: missing, invalid or outdated token.
* **403** `tenant_context_denied`: an API-key token, no admin role or `pulse.write`, or the tenant is outside your hierarchy.
* **404** `tenant_context_not_found`: the tenant has no policy.

parameters.name: tenantId
parameters.description: The tenant: a `tenant_id` from **List tenants** (`GET /v1/msp/admin/tenants`). Must be your own tenant or one beneath it.

put.description:
Replaces a tenant's sign-in policy. It applies to that tenant only, not the tenants beneath it.
**Needs a signed-in user's token.** API-key tokens from `POST /v1/auth/client-token` are rejected. The user needs `pulse.write` and an admin role.

* **400** `auth_request_invalid`: an invalid `mfa_requirement`, `allowed_mfa_methods` or `expected_version`.
* **401** `invalid_credentials`: missing, invalid or outdated token.
* **403** `tenant_context_denied`: an API-key token, no admin role or `pulse.write`, or the tenant is outside your hierarchy.
* **404** `tenant_context_not_found`: the tenant has no policy.
* **409** `policy_version_conflict`: the policy changed since you read it. Read it again and retry.
* **409** `require_sso_needs_sso_session`: turning on `require_sso` needs you to be signed in to this tenant with SSO.

parameters.name: tenantId
parameters.description: The tenant: a `tenant_id` from **List tenants** (`GET /v1/msp/admin/tenants`). Must be your own tenant or one beneath it.

get.description: Lists every country, ordered by name. Send a country's `id` as `country_id`. Needs `pulse.read`; returns 401 (no body) otherwise.
Lists the industries a tenant can have. Send an industry's `id` as `industry_id`. Needs `pulse.read`; returns 401 (no body) otherwise.
Lists the currencies prices can be shown in, ordered by code. Send a currency's `code` as `display_currency_code`. Needs `pulse.read`; returns 401 (no body) otherwise.
Lists the tenant types. Send a type's `id` as `tenant_type_id` when you provision a tenant. Needs `pulse.read`; returns 401 (no body) otherwise.

post.description:
Creates a tenant and queues the job that deploys it. The tenant starts in status
`provisioning` and becomes `active` when the job reaches `deployed`. Needs `pulse.write`.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header (or `idempotency_key` in the body) so a retry after a
timeout returns the original result instead of creating a second tenant.

* **400**: `invalid_provisioning_request` when `name` or `parent_tenant_id` is missing, or a validation problem naming the field.
* **401** (no body): missing or invalid token, no `pulse.write`, or `parent_tenant_id` is outside your hierarchy.
* **409**: no hosting capacity is available right now; try again later.

get.description:
Returns the current state of a create or decommission job. Poll it until `status` is
`deployed`, `decommissioned` or `failed`. Needs `pulse.write`.

* **401** (no body): missing or invalid token, no `pulse.write`, or the job's tenant is outside your hierarchy.
* **404** (no body): no job has this id.

parameters.name: jobId
parameters.description: The job: a `job_id` from **Provision a tenant** or **Decommission a tenant**.

post.description:
Queues the removal of a tenant. The tenant is disabled at once, and becomes `deleted` when
the job reaches `decommissioned`; poll **Get a provisioning job's status** with `job_id`.
Needs `pulse.write`. The request body is required: send `{}` if you have nothing to put in it.

Every tenant beneath this one must be suspended, disabled or deleted first. If a
decommission is already in progress for the tenant, that job is returned instead of a new one.
An `Idempotency-Key` header, when sent, takes precedence over `idempotency_key` in the body.

* **400**: `tenant: ["has_active_tenants"]` while a tenant beneath it is still active or provisioning.
* **401** (no body): missing or invalid token, no `pulse.write`, or the tenant is outside your hierarchy.

parameters.name: tenantId
parameters.description: The tenant to decommission: a `tenant_id` from **List tenants** (`GET /v1/msp/admin/tenants`).

post.description:
Suspends an active tenant: its users and API keys can no longer get new tokens until it is
reactivated. Takes effect immediately. Set `include_descendants` to suspend every active
tenant beneath it too. Needs `pulse.write`.

* **401** (no body): missing or invalid token, no `pulse.write`, the tenant is outside your hierarchy, or it is your own tenant.
* **409** `tenant_not_active`: the tenant is neither active nor already suspended (for example it is still provisioning).

parameters.name: tenantId
parameters.description: The tenant to suspend: a `tenant_id` from **List tenants** (`GET /v1/msp/admin/tenants`). It cannot be your own tenant.

post.description:
Reactivates a suspended tenant. Takes effect immediately. Set `include_descendants` to
reactivate every suspended tenant beneath it too. Needs `pulse.write`.

* **401** (no body): missing or invalid token, no `pulse.write`, the tenant is outside your hierarchy, or it is your own tenant.
* **409** `tenant_not_suspended`: the tenant is neither suspended nor already active.

parameters.name: tenantId
parameters.description: The tenant to reactivate: a `tenant_id` from **List tenants** (`GET /v1/msp/admin/tenants`). It cannot be your own tenant.

get.summary: List technicians who can be assigned to a tenant
get.description:
Lists the users who can be assigned as technician to a tenant you are about to provision:
enabled users with write access to `parent_tenant_id` that also covers the tenants beneath it.
Needs `pulse.write`.

* **400**: `parent_tenant_id: ["required"]` when it is missing.
* **401** (no body): missing or invalid token, no `pulse.write`, or `parent_tenant_id` is outside your hierarchy.

parameters.name: parent_tenant_id
parameters.description: The `parent_tenant_id` you will send to **Provision a tenant**.

get.description:
Lists a tenant and every tenant beneath it, ordered by name. Needs `pulse.read`.

* **400**: `page` must be 1–100000, `page_size` 1–100 and `search` at most 100 characters; otherwise 400 with `paging: ["invalid"]`. An unknown `kind` or `status` returns `kind: ["unsupported"]` or `status: ["unsupported"]`.
* **401** (no body): missing or invalid token, no `pulse.read`, or `root_tenant_id` is outside your hierarchy.

parameters.name: root_tenant_id
parameters.description: List this tenant and the tenants beneath it. Defaults to your own tenant. Must be your own tenant or one beneath it.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Matches tenants whose name, short name or host contains this text, ignoring case.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Only tenants of this kind: `organization` | `customer` | `tenant`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only tenants in this state: `active` | `provisioning` | `suspended` | `disabled` | `deleted`. When omitted, every state is included, deleted tenants too.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at `1` (the default).

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Tenants per page: `1`–`100`, default `50`.

get.description:
Lists the users who can be assigned as technician to an existing tenant: enabled users with
write access to the tenant, either on the tenant itself or inherited from a tenant above it.
Ordered by name. Needs `pulse.read`.

* **400**: `page` must be 1–100000, `page_size` 1–100 and `search` at most 100 characters; otherwise 400 with `paging: ["invalid"]`.
* **401** (no body): missing or invalid token, no `pulse.read`, or `tenant_id` is outside your hierarchy.

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: Required. The tenant you want to assign a technician to.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Matches technicians whose first name, last name or email contains this text, ignoring case.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at `1` (the default).

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Technicians per page: `1`–`100`, default `50`.

get.description:
Lists the users with access to a tenant or any tenant beneath it, ordered by email unless
`sort` is given. A user with access to several tenants appears once per tenant. Needs `pulse.read`.

* **400**: `page` must be 1–100000, `page_size` 1–100 and `search` at most 100 characters; otherwise 400 with `paging: ["invalid"]`. An unknown `status` or `sort` returns `["unsupported"]` under that name.
* **401** (no body): missing or invalid token, no `pulse.read`, or `tenant_id` is outside your hierarchy.

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: List users of this tenant and the tenants beneath it. Defaults to your own tenant. Must be your own tenant or one beneath it.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Matches users whose email, first name, last name or tenant name contains this text, ignoring case.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only `active` users (who can sign in) or only `disabled` users.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: `login_asc`, `login_desc`, `status_asc` or `status_desc`. The login sorts order by `last_login_at`: users who never signed in come first with `login_asc` and last with `login_desc`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at `1` (the default).

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Items per page: `1`–`100`, default `50`.

post.description:
Creates a user and gives them a role on one tenant. Returns 201 with the new user.
**Needs a signed-in user's token.** API-key tokens from `POST /v1/auth/client-token` are rejected. The user needs `pulse.write` and an admin role.

* **400**: a validation problem naming the field, or `password_rejected` / `email_rejected` when the password or email is not accepted.
* **401** `invalid_credentials`: missing, invalid or outdated token, or an API-key token.
* **403** `tenant_context_denied`: no admin role or `pulse.write`, or `tenant_id` is outside your hierarchy.
* **404** `tenant_context_not_found`: `tenant_id` does not exist.
* **409** `email_taken`: another user already has this email.
* **502** `legacy_provisioning_failed`: the tenant's own server could not create the user; try again later.

get.description:
Returns one user and their first access grant within `tenant_id` and the tenants beneath it.
Needs `pulse.read`.

* **401** (no body): missing or invalid token, no `pulse.read`, or `tenant_id` is outside your hierarchy.
* **404** (no body): the user has no access within that part of the hierarchy.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: The user: a `user_id` from **List users** (`GET /v1/msp/admin/users`).

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: Look for the user within this tenant and the tenants beneath it. Defaults to your own tenant.

patch.description:
Changes a user's name, email, password, role, tenant or whether they can sign in, and returns
the updated user. **Needs a signed-in user's token.** API-key tokens from `POST /v1/auth/client-token` are rejected. The user needs `pulse.write` and an admin role.

* **400**: a validation problem naming the field, or `password_rejected` / `email_rejected`.
* **401** `invalid_credentials`: missing, invalid or outdated token, or an API-key token.
* **403** `tenant_context_denied`: no admin role or `pulse.write`, or a tenant involved is outside your hierarchy.
* **404**: the user does not exist, or `tenant_id` does not exist (`tenant_context_not_found`).
* **409** `email_taken`: another user already has this email.
* **409** `last_admin_required`: the change would leave a tenant without an administrator.
* **409** `mfa_state_changed`: the user was changed at the same time; retry.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: The user: a `user_id` from **List users** (`GET /v1/msp/admin/users`).

delete.description:
Disables a user: they lose access to every tenant and can no longer sign in. The user is not
deleted. Returns 204. **Needs a signed-in user's token.** API-key tokens from `POST /v1/auth/client-token` are rejected. The user needs `pulse.write` and an admin role.

* **401** `invalid_credentials`: missing, invalid or outdated token, or an API-key token.
* **403** `tenant_context_denied`: no admin role or `pulse.write`, or the user has access to a tenant outside your hierarchy.
* **404** `tenant_context_not_found`: the user does not exist or is already disabled.
* **409** `last_admin_required`: the user is the last administrator of a tenant.
* **409** `mfa_state_changed`: the user was changed at the same time; retry.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: The user: a `user_id` from **List users** (`GET /v1/msp/admin/users`).

post.description:
Removes all of a user's MFA methods and recovery codes, for example after they lose their
phone. Returns 204. **Needs a signed-in user's token.** API-key tokens from `POST /v1/auth/client-token` are rejected. The user needs `pulse.write` and an admin role.

* **400** `auth_request_invalid`: `reason` is missing or longer than 160 characters.
* **401** `invalid_credentials`: missing, invalid or outdated token, or an API-key token.
* **403** `tenant_context_denied`: no admin role or `pulse.write`, or the user has access to a tenant outside your hierarchy.
* **404** `tenant_context_not_found`: the user does not exist or is disabled.
* **409** `last_admin_required`: the user is the only administrator of a tenant.
* **409** `mfa_state_changed`: the user was changed at the same time; retry.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: The user: a `user_id` from **List users** (`GET /v1/msp/admin/users`).

get.description:
Lists the roles you can give a user. Send a role's `key` as `role` when you create or update
a user. Needs `pulse.read`; returns 401 (no body) otherwise.

code.description: What went wrong, for example `tenant_context_denied` or `email_taken`. Each operation lists the codes it returns.

trace_id.description: An id for this request. Quote it when you contact support.

denied_scopes.description: The scopes that were refused. Only present on some sign-in errors.

attempts_remaining.description: How many attempts are left before a lockout. Only present on some sign-in errors.

retry_after_seconds.description: How long to wait before retrying. Only present on some sign-in errors.

AuthProblemDetails.description: An error from the user, sign-in policy and token endpoints. Branch on `code`, not on the text.

idempotency_key.description:
A unique value, such as a UUID v4, that you generate per decommission. Retrying with a key
that was already accepted returns the original job instead of queuing another. An
`Idempotency-Key` header, when sent, takes precedence over this field.

DecommissionApiRequest.description: Send `{}` when you do not use an idempotency key: the body itself is required.

items.description: Every eligible technician, sorted by name. The list is not paged.

user_id.description: The technician's user id. Send it as `assigned_technician_user_id` when you provision a tenant.

display_name.description: The technician's first and last name.

email.description: The technician's email. Null when they have none.

type.description: A URI reference that identifies the kind of error.

title.description: A short summary of the error, or its code.

detail.description: More detail about this occurrence, when there is any.

instance.description: A URI reference that identifies this occurrence, when there is one.

errors.description: The invalid fields, each with one or more error codes.

HttpValidationProblemDetails.description:
A 400 validation error. `errors` maps each invalid field to error codes, for example
`{"industry_id": ["unsupported"]}`. Each request schema lists the codes its fields can return.

client_id.description: The API key's client id, which starts with `pc_`.

client_secret.description: The API key's secret, which starts with `pcs_`. It is shown only once, when the key is created.

requested_scopes.description:
The scopes the token should carry: `pulse.read`, `pulse.write`, or both.

**When omitted, the token gets `pulse.read` only**, even if the key also holds
`pulse.write`. Provisioning, suspend, reactivate, decommission, job status, updates and user
management all need `pulse.write`, so ask for it explicitly. Asking for a scope the key
does not hold returns 403 `scope_denied`.

MachineClientTokenRequest.description: Exchanges an API key (client id and secret) for a bearer token for the key's own tenant.

expires_in.description: Seconds until the token expires: `3600` (one hour) by default.

expires_at.description: When the token expires: an ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC (offset `+00:00`).

MachineClientTokenResponse.description: A bearer token. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`. There is no refresh token: request a new one before `expires_at`.

reason.description: Why the MFA methods are being reset, kept in the audit log. Required, at most 160 characters; otherwise 400 `auth_request_invalid`.

user_id.description: The technician's user id. Send it as `assigned_technician_user_id` when you update the tenant.

name.description: The technician's first and last name, or their email when no name is set.

email.description: The technician's email, in lower case. Null when they have none.

items.description: The technicians on this page. Empty when nothing matches.

page.description: The page number returned, starting at `1`.

page_size.description: The maximum number of technicians per page, as requested (default `50`, maximum `100`).

total_count.description: The number of technicians that match across all pages.

MspAdminTechnicianPageResponse.description: One page of technicians, ordered by name.

tenant_id.description: The tenant's id. Use it as `tenantId` or `parent_tenant_id` in the other endpoints.

tenant_host.description: The tenant's host name, for example `cc2080fe.cyrisma.com`.

short_name.description: The tenant's short display name. Null when none is set.

kind.description:
Where the tenant sits in the hierarchy: `organization` | `customer` | `tenant`.
The CYRISMA top-level tenant is `root`.

parent_tenant_id.description: The tenant directly above this one. Null for the top of the hierarchy.

industry_id.description: The tenant's industry: an `id` from **List industries** (`GET /v1/msp/admin/lookups/industries`). Null when not set.

industry_name.description: The name of `industry_id`. Null when not set.

tenant_type_id.description:
The tenant type: an `id` from **List tenant types** (`GET /v1/msp/admin/lookups/tenant-types`).
Null when not set.

Values:
* `0` for MSP
* `1` for MSSP
* `2` for Reseller
* `3` for Client

tenant_type_name.description: The name of `tenant_type_id`, for example `Client`. Null when not set.

assigned_technician_user_id.description: The user id of the technician responsible for this tenant. Null when no technician is assigned.

assigned_technician_name.description: The assigned technician's name, or their email when no name is set. An empty string when no technician is assigned.

assigned_technician_email.description: The assigned technician's email, in lower case. Null when no technician is assigned or they have no email.

provisioning_status.description:
The status of the tenant's most recent provisioning job, which may be a create, decommission
or restore: `queued` | `leased` | `running` | `deployed` | `decommissioned` | `failed`.
Null for tenants that have never had a job, such as tenants migrated from the legacy platform.

instance_path.description: The tenant names from the top of the list (`root_tenant_id`, or your own tenant) down to this tenant, joined with `/`.

created_at.description: When the tenant was created: an ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC (offset `+00:00`), for example `2026-09-16T15:06:58.10164+00:00`.

updated_at.description: When the tenant's record last changed: an ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC (offset `+00:00`), for example `2026-09-16T15:06:58.10164+00:00`.

MspAdminTenantListItem.description: A summary of one tenant. Call **Get a tenant** (`GET /v1/msp/admin/tenants/{tenantId}`) with `tenant_id` for its full details.

items.description: The tenants on this page. Empty when nothing matches the filters.

page.description: The page number returned, starting at `1`.

page_size.description: The maximum number of tenants per page, as requested (default `50`, maximum `100`).

total_count.description: The number of tenants that match the filters across all pages.

MspAdminTenantPageResponse.description:
One page of tenants, ordered by name. Keep requesting the next `page` while
`page * page_size` is less than `total_count`.

tenant_id.description: The tenant the user gets access to, including every tenant beneath it. Must be your own tenant or one beneath it.

first_name.description: The user's first name. Required; at most 100 characters, and at most 200 together with `last_name`. Otherwise 400 with `first_name: ["invalid"]`.

email.description:
The user's email, which is also their login id. Stored in lower case. An invalid address
returns 400 with `email: ["invalid"]`; an email already used by any user returns 409 `email_taken`.

password.description:
The user's password: at least 12 characters, with an upper-case letter, a lower-case letter,
a digit and a symbol. Missing returns 400 with `password: ["required"]`; too weak returns
400 `password_rejected`.

role.description:
The user's role: a `key` from **List assignable user roles** (`GET /v1/msp/admin/user-roles`).
Admin roles can make changes; reader roles can only view. Any other value returns 400 with
`role: ["unsupported"]`.

MspAdminUserCreateRequest.description:
Creates a user with access to one tenant. The user can sign in straight away with the
password you set; no invitation email is sent. Validation failures return 400 with the field
names as keys, for example `{"email": ["invalid"]}`.

items.description: The users on this page. Empty when nothing matches.

page.description: The page number returned, starting at `1`.

page_size.description: The maximum number of items per page, as requested (default `50`, maximum `100`).

total_count.description: The number of items that match across all pages.

MspAdminUserPageResponse.description:
One page of users, ordered by email. There is one item per user and tenant, so a user with
access to several tenants appears more than once, and `total_count` counts those items.

user_id.description: The user's id. Use it as `userId` in the other user endpoints.

last_name.description: The user's last name. An empty string when none is set.

display_name.description: The user's full name, or their email when no name is set.

email.description: The user's email, which is also their login id.

tenant_id.description: The tenant this access applies to (including the tenants beneath it).

roles.description: The user's role on this tenant: a `key` from **List assignable user roles**.

scopes.description: What the role allows: `pulse.login`, `pulse.read`, and `pulse.write` for admin roles.

status.description: `active` when the user can sign in; `disabled` when they have been disabled or are locked out.

last_login_at.description: When the user last signed in: an ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC (offset `+00:00`). Null if they never have.

selected_mfa_method.description: The MFA method the user chose: `email` or `totp`. Null when none is chosen.

enrolled_mfa_methods.description: The MFA methods the user has set up: `email`, `totp`, both, or none.

MspAdminUserResponse.description: A user and their access to one tenant.

key.description: The value to send as `role` when you create or update a user.

can_write.description: True for admin roles, which can make changes; false for reader roles, which can only view.

tenant_id.description: Moves the user's access to this tenant. Both the current and the new tenant must be your own tenant or beneath it.

last_name.description: The user's last name. An empty string removes it.

email.description:
The user's new email, which is also their login id. Changing it removes the user's email MFA
method. An email already used by another user returns 409 `email_taken`.

password.description: Sets a new password, with the same rules as when the user was created. Too weak returns 400 `password_rejected`.

role.description: The user's new role: a `key` from **List assignable user roles** (`GET /v1/msp/admin/user-roles`).

enabled.description:
`false` disables the user so they can no longer sign in; `true` lets a disabled user sign in
again. Disabling or demoting a tenant's last administrator returns 409 `last_admin_required`.

MspAdminUserUpdateRequest.description:
Send only the fields you want to change; omitted or null fields keep their current value.
The change applies to the user's first access grant (the one **Get a user** returns).

id.description: The ISO 3166-1 numeric country code, for example `840` for the United States. Send it as `country_id`.

code.description: The two-letter ISO 3166-1 country code, for example `US`.
The three-letter ISO 4217 currency code, for example `USD`. Send it as `display_currency_code`.

symbol.description: The currency symbol as a hexadecimal Unicode code point, for example `24` for $ and `20AC` for €. Currencies without a single symbol use their code, for example `CHF`.

id.description: The industry's id. Send it as `industry_id`.
The tenant type's id. Send it as `tenant_type_id` when you provision a tenant.

name.description: The tenant type's name, for example `Client`.

type.description: A URI reference that identifies the kind of error.

title.description: A short summary of the error, or its code.

detail.description: More detail about this occurrence, when there is any.

instance.description: A URI reference that identifies this occurrence, when there is one.

ProblemDetails.description: An error in the RFC 9457 problem format. Where an operation lists an error code, such as `tenant_not_active` or `scope_denied`, it is in `title`.

include_descendants.description:
When `true`, the change also applies to every tenant beneath this one, at any depth.
Defaults to `false`: only the tenant itself changes.

TenantAccessApiRequest.description: Optional: sending no body is the same as `{"include_descendants": false}`.

tenant_id.description: The tenant named in the request.

status.description: The status the call moves tenants to: `suspended` for suspend, `active` for reactivate.

changed_tenant_ids.description:
The tenants this call actually changed. Tenants that were already in the target state are
not listed, so the list is empty when nothing needed changing.

name.description: The name of the tenant. Trimmed; an empty value is ignored.

short_name.description:
A short display name, at most 70 characters. An empty string removes it.
A longer value returns 400 with `short_name: ["maximum_length_70"]`.

kind.description:
Where the tenant sits in the hierarchy: `organization` | `customer` | `tenant`.
Any other value returns 400 with `kind: ["unsupported"]`.

notification_email.description: The email address that receives notifications for this tenant.

address_1.description: First line of the tenant's street address.

address_2.description: Second line of the tenant's street address.

state.description: The tenant's state, province or region.

postal_code.description: The tenant's postal or ZIP code.

country_id.description:
The tenant's country: an `id` from **List countries** (`GET /v1/msp/admin/lookups/countries`).
An unknown id returns 400 with `country_id: ["unsupported"]`. Changing it does not move an
existing tenant to another hosting region.

industry_id.description:
The tenant's industry: an `id` from **List industries** (`GET /v1/msp/admin/lookups/industries`).
An unknown id returns 400 with `industry_id: ["unsupported"]`.

employee_count.description: The number of employees at the tenant. A negative number returns 400 with `employee_count: ["invalid"]`.

display_currency_code.description:
The currency the tenant's prices are shown in: a `code` from **List currencies**
(`GET /v1/msp/admin/lookups/currencies`). Case-insensitive. An unknown code returns 400 with
`display_currency_code: ["unsupported"]`.

assigned_technician_user_id.description:
The technician responsible for this tenant: a `user_id` from **List technicians**
(`GET /v1/msp/admin/technicians?tenant_id=…`) called with this tenant's id. Anyone else
returns 400 with `assigned_technician_user_id: ["ineligible"]`.

mdr_xdr_tenant_id.description: The tenant's id in the linked MDR/XDR service.

trial.description:
Send `false` to end a trial and make the tenant a full tenant; it has no effect on a tenant
that is not a trial. A tenant cannot be turned back into a trial: `true` returns 400 with
`trial: ["one_way"]`.

TenantAdminMetadataPatch.description:
Send only the fields you want to change. A field that is omitted or null keeps its current
value, so fields cannot be cleared this way; the one exception is `short_name`, which an
empty string removes. The tenant type and the assigned technician cannot be removed here.

Validation failures return 400 with the field name as the key, for example
`{"country_id": ["unsupported"]}`. Only the first failure is reported.

tenant_id.description: The tenant's id. Use it as `tenantId` or `parent_tenant_id` in the other endpoints.

tenant_host.description: The tenant's host name, for example `cc2080fe.cyrisma.com`.

short_name.description: The tenant's short display name. Null when none is set.

kind.description:
Where the tenant sits in the hierarchy: `organization` | `customer` | `tenant`.
The CYRISMA top-level tenant is `root`.

scope_version.description: A counter that increases whenever the tenants beneath this one change, for example when a tenant is created under it. Most integrations can ignore it.

notification_email.description: The email address that receives notifications for this tenant.

address_1.description: First line of the tenant's street address.

address_2.description: Second line of the tenant's street address.

state.description: The tenant's state, province or region.

postal_code.description: The tenant's postal or ZIP code.

country_id.description: The tenant's country: an `id` from **List countries** (`GET /v1/msp/admin/lookups/countries`).

industry_id.description: The tenant's industry: an `id` from **List industries** (`GET /v1/msp/admin/lookups/industries`). Null when not set.

industry_name.description: The name of `industry_id`. Null when not set.

tenant_type_id.description:
The tenant type: an `id` from **List tenant types** (`GET /v1/msp/admin/lookups/tenant-types`).
Null when not set.

Values:
* `0` for MSP
* `1` for MSSP
* `2` for Reseller
* `3` for Client

tenant_type_name.description: The name of `tenant_type_id`, for example `Client`. Null when not set.

employee_count.description: The number of employees at the tenant.

legacy_assigned_technician_user_id.description: The assigned technician's user id in the legacy CYRISMA platform, kept for migrated tenants. Use `assigned_technician_user_id` instead.

assigned_technician_user_id.description: The user id of the technician responsible for this tenant. Null when no technician is assigned.

assigned_technician_name.description: The assigned technician's name, or their email when no name is set. Null when no technician is assigned.

assigned_technician_email.description: The assigned technician's email, in lower case. Null when no technician is assigned or they have no email.

mdr_xdr_tenant_id.description: The tenant's id in the linked MDR/XDR service. Null when none is linked.

display_currency_code.description: The currency the tenant's prices are shown in: a `code` from **List currencies** (`GET /v1/msp/admin/lookups/currencies`). Defaults to `USD`.

provisioning_status.description:
The status of the tenant's most recent provisioning job, which may be a create, decommission
or restore: `queued` | `leased` | `running` | `deployed` | `decommissioned` | `failed`.
Null for tenants that have never had a job, such as tenants migrated from the legacy platform.

trial.description: True when the tenant is a 21-day trial tenant.

created_at.description: When the tenant was created: an ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC (offset `+00:00`), for example `2026-09-16T15:06:58.10164+00:00`.

updated_at.description: When the tenant's record last changed: an ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC (offset `+00:00`), for example `2026-09-16T15:06:58.10164+00:00`.

TenantAdminMetadataResponse.description: The full details of one tenant.

mfa_requirement.description:
Whether users must use multi-factor authentication: `disabled` | `required`.

* `required`: every user must complete MFA, and users without a method are asked to set one up.
* `disabled`: MFA is not forced, but users who have already set up a method are still asked for it.

allowed_mfa_methods.description: The MFA methods users may use: one or both of `email` and `totp` (an authenticator app). Must not be empty or repeat a value.

expected_version.description:
The `version` from your last read of the policy. If someone changed the policy since, the
call returns 409 `policy_version_conflict`: read it again and retry.

require_sso.description:
When `true`, users must sign in with the tenant's single sign-on. Defaults to `false`.
Turning it on returns 409 `require_sso_needs_sso_session` unless you are signed in to this
tenant with SSO yourself, so you cannot lock yourself out.

TenantAuthPolicyPutRequest.description:
Replaces the whole policy: send every field, because an omitted `require_sso` is saved as
`false`. Invalid values return 400 `auth_request_invalid`.

Tightening the policy (making MFA required, or removing an allowed method) signs every user
of the tenant out: their existing tokens stop working.

tenant_id.description: The tenant the policy belongs to.

mfa_requirement.description: Whether users must use multi-factor authentication: `disabled` | `required`. New tenants start with `disabled`.

allowed_mfa_methods.description: The MFA methods users may use: `email`, `totp` (an authenticator app), or both. New tenants allow both.

version.description: The policy's version. Send it as `expected_version` when you update the policy.

updated_at.description: When the policy last changed: an ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC (offset `+00:00`).

require_sso.description: True when users must sign in with the tenant's single sign-on.

TenantAuthPolicyResponse.description: How users of one tenant sign in. The policy applies to that tenant only; tenants beneath it keep their own.

parent_tenant_id.description:
The tenant the new tenant is created under. It must be your own tenant or one of its
descendants; any other tenant returns 401. Use `tenant_id` from **List tenants**
(`GET /v1/msp/admin/tenants`).

name.description: The name of the tenant. Leading and trailing spaces are trimmed; a blank name returns 400 `invalid_provisioning_request`.

short_name.description:
A short display name for the tenant, at most 70 characters.
A longer value returns 400 with `short_name: ["maximum_length_70"]`.

kind.description:
Tenant kind.

Allowed values: `organization` | `tenant`. Defaults to `tenant`.

notification_email.description: The email address that receives notifications for this tenant.

address_1.description: First line of the tenant's street address.

address_2.description: Second line of the tenant's street address.

state.description: The tenant's state, province or region.

postal_code.description: The tenant's postal or ZIP code.

country_id.description:
The tenant's country. Use `id` from **List countries** (`GET /v1/msp/admin/lookups/countries`).

The country also decides where the tenant is hosted and its data is stored. When it is
omitted, the tenant is hosted in the same region as its parent.

industry_id.description:
The tenant's industry. Use `id` from **List industries** (`GET /v1/msp/admin/lookups/industries`).
An unknown id returns 400 with `industry_id: ["unsupported"]`.

employee_count.description: The number of employees at the tenant. Defaults to `1`.

assigned_technician_user_id.description:
The technician responsible for this tenant. Use `user_id` from **List technicians who can be
assigned to a tenant** (`GET /v1/msp/provisioning/eligible-technicians?parent_tenant_id=…`),
called with the same `parent_tenant_id`. Anyone else returns 400 with
`assigned_technician_user_id: ["ineligible"]`.

tenant_type_id.description:
Represents the tenant type, which can be obtained from **List tenant types**
(`GET /v1/msp/admin/lookups/tenant-types`); send its `id`.

Allowed values:
* `0` for MSP
* `1` for MSSP
* `2` for Reseller
* `3` for Client

Any other value returns 400 with `tenant_type_id: ["unsupported"]`.

support_enabled.description: Support enabled for tenant. Defaults to `true`.

idempotency_key.description:
A unique value, such as a UUID v4, that you generate for each tenant you create. Retrying a
request with a key that was already accepted returns the original result instead of creating
a second tenant, so a timed-out request is safe to retry. An `Idempotency-Key` header, when
sent, takes precedence over this field.

TenantProvisioningCreateApiRequest.description:
Creates a tenant under `parent_tenant_id` and queues the job that deploys it. The response
carries the new `tenant_id` and a `job_id`; poll **Get a provisioning job's status**
(`GET /v1/msp/provisioning/jobs/{jobId}`) until the job reaches `deployed`.

Only `parent_tenant_id`, `name` and `trial` are required. Validation failures return 400 with
the offending field names as keys, for example `{"industry_id": ["unsupported"]}`.

tenant_id.description: The tenant the job is for. After a create, use it as `tenantId` in the other endpoints.

tenant_number.description: The tenant's number, as shown to support staff.

job_id.description: The job's id. Pass it to **Get a provisioning job's status**.

status.description:
The job's status: `queued` | `leased` | `running` | `deployed` | `decommissioned` | `failed`.

* `queued`: accepted, waiting for a worker. A new create or decommission always starts here.
* `leased` / `running`: a worker has picked it up.
* `deployed`: the tenant is ready and its status is now `active`.
* `decommissioned`: the tenant is removed and its status is now `deleted`.
* `failed`: the job did not complete.

tenant_host.description: The tenant's host name, for example `cc4a1b2c.cyrisma.com`.

registration_key.description: The tenant's agent registration key: 32 upper-case hexadecimal characters. Agents installed for this tenant register with it.

orchestrator_wake_succeeded.description: Internal. Always null in these responses; ignore it.

TenantProvisioningCreateApiResponse.description:
A tenant lifecycle job, returned by **Provision a tenant**, **Get a provisioning job's status**
and **Decommission a tenant**. Jobs run asynchronously: poll **Get a provisioning job's status**
(`GET /v1/msp/provisioning/jobs/{jobId}`) with `job_id` until `status` is `deployed` (create),
`decommissioned` (decommission) or `failed`.

bearerAuth.description: A machine-client token from POST /v1/auth/client-token. Reads need the pulse.read scope; provisioning and tenant updates need pulse.write, which the token only carries when requested_scopes asks for it. Creating, changing, disabling and resetting MFA for users, and the tenant sign-in policy, need a signed-in user's token instead: they reject API-key tokens.
